articles.title: Criminal probe underway over would-be spoiler Senate candidate in Alaska
articles.summary: By Andrew Goudsward and Nathan Frandino WASHINGTON/ANCHORAGE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration stepped up criminal and civil investigations into allegations that Democrats conspired to recruit a spoiler candidate in a critical Senate race in Alaska, officials said on Friday, injecting fresh uncertainty into Tuesday's midterm elections. The top federal prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said ‌at a press conference that a Wednesday New York Times article about the effort had driven a "surge" of FBI resources, adding that he had assigned several prosecutors to the case ‌and that investigative steps were taking place "intensely and swiftly." "Every Alaskan deserves a fair election, and they're going to get one," he said. "Anyone who tries to illegally deceive voters and interfere with the election, they'll answer for it." The Alaska contest is widely ​seen as one of the US Senate races that could sway control of the chamber, now narrowly held by Trump's Republicans. TRUMP ORDERED SUIT, CLAIMS 'FRAUD AT HIGHEST LEVEL' The Justice Department's legal actions in Alaska and California, where the Trump administration is trying to prevent some ballots from being counted, represent an extraordinary federal intervention in state-run elections, which are administered locally under the US Constitution. When the DOJ filed the civil suit against Alaska a week ago, Trump told reporters, "I'm the one that said do it." Heyman declined to offer specifics when asked what possible crimes were being examined, saying he would let the Alaska investigation proceed, although Trump has called for a ‌prosecution of Senate candidate Mary Peltola, a Democrat. "This is voter fraud at the ⁠highest level," Trump told a Florida rally on Friday. The Department of Justice asked a federal judge on Friday to ensure the preservation of ballots that "may be impacted by voter confusion." The court filing requested the judge's help obtaining documents from the Democratic campaign and others to determine "whether Daniel J. Sullivan’s candidacy is frivolous ⁠or fraudulent." The DOJ also has sued Alaska to preemptively block the state from certifying the results of the Senate race if the Republican incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, loses due to the presence of a third candidate, named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. It is not clear what, if any, laws may have been broken. Both parties have engaged in "ballot stacking" by propping up lesser-known candidates to siphon votes from their opponents. If Democrats take one or both chambers of Congress, ​they ​intend to launch investigations of the Trump administration and increase pressure on the president to end the war against Iran. The ​New York Times reported this week that staffers from the Peltola campaign and ‌the Democratic Party's Senate campaign arm helped recruit Daniel J. Sullivan Jr, a retired teacher living in a remote fishing village, to appear on the ballot. Reuters has not independently confirmed the Times' reporting. Peltola has denied knowing about any effort to recruit the second Sullivan, and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has also denied involvement. The retired teacher has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign. SURGE OF VOTING NATIONWIDE DESPITE UNCERTAINTY Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are bracing for further disruptions from the Trump administration, which has sued about 30 states seeking unredacted voter rolls. “The new tactic is just to create enough confusion and enough uncertainty and enough doubt through the filing of all these lawsuits to lay the groundwork to ultimately, I think, challenge the results once the dust settles after Tuesday," said Jonathan Diaz of the ‌nonpartisan Campaign Legal Center. Trump has long sought to sow distrust of election results, falsely claiming for years that his ​2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Biden was the result of widespread fraud. Voter fraud in the US is extremely rare, studies ​and investigations have found. Despite any uncertainty, a record 49 million people have cast early ballots, ​more than any other midterm election in US history, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, with even the American-born Pope Leo casting a ballot ‌by mail. The DOJ has also pushed forward a legal case in California, issuing ​subpoenas to election officials as part of a criminal ​probe into alleged voting by noncitizens, according to copies of documents seen by Reuters. A US appeals court on Friday rejected the department's request to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens, the second time the court has done so this week. A lower court judge had denied the ​administration's request, finding it would potentially disenfranchise thousands of legal voters. Trump said ‌on Friday he would attend weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas, a day after canceling them, telling reporters at the White House that Republicans in those states had called ​him and asked him to reconsider. (Additional reporting by Jarrett Renshaw, Nathan Layne, Jana Winter, Max Schwarz, Kia Johnson, Maria Tsvetkova, Doina Chiacu, Jan Wolfe and David Morgan; Writing ​by Joseph Ax and Daniel Trotta; Editing by Jesse Mesner-Hage, Scott Malone, Alistair Bell and Rosalba O'Brien) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-escalates-legal-challenges-against-101126175.html

articles.title: DOJ warned election workers in all 50 states. Now a judge has stepped in.
articles.summary: A federal judge on Friday ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening state and local election officials with criminal prosecution over their handling of disputes about voter qualifications. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson also ordered the Trump administration to cease demanding that election workers remove voters from statewide rolls, refuse to issue ballots to specific voters or segregate ballots cast in the midterms based on the administration's claims that some voters are ineligible. "Because the public has a paramount interest in ensuring that election officials and workers are able to carry out their work in accordance with federal law and election procedure, and the official day of the Elections is only a couple of days away, the balance of the equities and public interest weigh in Plaintiffs' favor," Thompson wrote. Thompson, a San Francisco-based Biden appointee, issued the temporary restraining order in connection with a lawsuit brought by the Service Employees International Union and other groups. Her directive also requires the DOJ to reach out to any state or local officials who received warnings about possible prosecution and inform them that "demands and threats of prosecution to election officials and workers … have been enjoined." The Justice Department on Thursday sent letters to election workers in all 50 states alluding to possible prosecution if they didn't preserve election records. DOJ did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the judge's broad ruling. Thompson's order effectively enforces a stern warning issued to the Trump administration by another California-based federal judge, David Carter, earlier this week. "These threats must stop," Carter wrote in a ruling that threw out the Justice Department's effort to compel California to set aside any ballots cast by up to 20,000 people federal officials had identified as likely noncitizens. The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday declined to set aside Carter's order. Thompson's new directive also follows an order by U.S. District Judge James Boasberg, chief of the federal district court in Washington, D.C., to require the Trump administration to provide the list of those 20,000 purported noncitizens to an immigrant advocacy group. Boasberg's order was rooted, in part, on the group's claim that the Trump administration's threats were influencing the conduct of state and local elected officials. articles.title: Stocks plunge on the final trading day of October as AI reckoning grips Wall Street
articles.summary: US stocks plunged in the final trading day of the month as earnings from Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) this week rekindled concerns about the amount of money Big Tech is spending on its AI ambitions. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 2.8% as a tech-fueled sell-off intensified. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 1.2%, or over 650 points, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) dropped 2%. For the month, the Dow gained 1.5%, while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 gave up gains, falling 5.2% and 1.2%, respectively. October marked the worst month for the Nasdaq since March 2025. Stocks fell for the second day in a row after Amazon and Alphabet posted rare earnings misses , renewing concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Amazon shares fell 2%, while Alphabet continued to erase market value after its stock suffered its worst day in over 20 years. Intel ( INTC ) also suffered a brutal reaction to its earnings report, dropping 29% in premarket trading after the company's Q4 outlook came up short. One bright spot in the market was ExxonMobil ( XOM ) and Chevron ( CVX ), whose stocks briefly touched record highs after the oil majors reported that their earnings were boosted as refining margins widened amid the war in the Middle East. Pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca ( AZN ) also reported an earnings beat before the opening bell. While earnings remain in focus, oil prices rebounded higher, putting additional pressure on markets. Brent crude futures ( BZ=F ) rose to $112 per barrel, while WTI crude ( CL=F ) reached $104 per barrel. Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) prices tumbled more than 2% as crypto assets were rattled following a $6.3 billion hack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, marking the largest heist of its kind in history. articles.title: Election forecasters shift 12 more House races toward Democrats before Tuesday
articles.summary: It's crunch time. With just days to go until the 2026 midterm elections, Democratic and Republican candidates for the U.S. House of Representatives nationwide are making one last push to persuade voters in their districts — and help their party win or retain control of the chamber on Nov. 3. The stakes are high. President Trump has enjoyed complete Republican control of Congress for the first half of his second term. Flipping the House would give Democrats the power to block parts of the president's agenda, investigate his administration and even impeach him (again) . Historically speaking, a president's party almost always loses seats when voters return to the polls to judge his first two years in office. (The average number lost since World War II? Twenty-six .) Sometimes, the backlash is so pervasive that the president's party loses seats across a wide range of competitive districts — a phenomenon known as a "wave" election. But the past doesn't necessarily predict the future, and Republicans have certain advantages today that they didn't have before. Here's what needs to happen for each party to come out on top. The races to watch The first thing to know about any House election is that while all 435 congressional districts are technically up for grabs, roughly 80% of those contests (representing about 350 seats) are not considered competitive. House incumbents have always had huge advantages: money and name recognition, mostly. But their head start has only widened in recent years as partisan polarization and redistricting have helped make the vast majority of congressional districts "safe" for one party . These days, incumbents tend to focus more on fending off primary challengers. The general election can be a breeze in comparison. As a result, this year's true battleground is relatively small. According to the nonpartisan Cook Political Report's " race ratings ," just 18 contests are genuine "tossups" at this point. Another 18 "lean Democratic," and 17 "lean Republican." There's also a third competitive category that includes 18 seats where Democrats are the "likely" winners, and 14 seats where the same could be said about Republicans. That's 85 competitive districts — again, out of 435. It’s clear from looking at those ratings which party is playing more defense and which is playing more offense — and where. Only 30 Democratic-held seats are considered competitive, and more than half of them (17) are "likely" to remain Democratic, according to Cook. Just four Democratic seats are toss ups. Just three are leaning Republican. In contrast, a full 55 Republican-held seats are considered competitive — and about half of them are tossups (14) or leaning Democratic (13). Geographically, this year's tossups are concentrated in certain kinds of places: Rust Belt districts in states that have swung from party to party in the past (such as Michigan, Pennsylvania and Ohio); Mid-Atlantic suburbs (in states such as New York, Virginia and North Carolina) where Trump has scrambled some of the usual coalitions; and Sun Belt districts (think Florida, Texas, California and Nevada) where Latinos factor heavily. Trump carried many of these areas in 2024 . On Friday, Cook shifted another dozen of its race ratings toward Democrats — part of a pattern that has seen the outlet move a total of 75 race ratings toward Democrats over the last month. “As the House battleground map has expanded, Democrats now have the potential to win their largest majority since 2009. President Donald Trump’s approval rating is underwater even in deep red seats that he won comfortably in 2024, and heavy spending from Republicans doesn’t appear to be moving the needle,”  Cook’s House analyst wrote. “While Democrats won’t reach the 257 seats they had following President Barack Obama’s election — a high water mark for them this century — they could surpass the majorities they had following the 2006 and 2018 blue wave cycles.” She went on to project that Democrats “will flip 12 to 25 seats, giving them as many as 240 seats in the House.” Overall, the map gives Democrats more pickup options — which means more paths to a House majority. The path to a Democratic House Senate and governor contests can be quirky — more state-specific and personality-driven. But national dynamics tend to play a larger role in shaping the composition of the incoming House. So it's not just a matter of who has more targets on the board. It's that the board itself tends to tilt to one side or the other, taking most of those targets with it. A recent example was the 2010 midterm election, when impatience with America's slow recovery from the 2008 financial collapse and frustration with President Barack Obama's response helped Republicans gain 64 House seats. Beyond the history of midterm backlash against the president's party, Democrats have two big advantages right now. One is that the current Republican majority is so minuscule — just 219 votes to 214, including an independent who caucuses with Republicans — that Democrats only need a net gain of three seats to win back the House. The other is that the board seems to be tilting in Democrats' favor — assuming the polls are right. Surveys suggest there's one underlying factor pulling the national electorate to the left: dissatisfaction with Trump. According to the data journalists at Silver Bulletin , an average of 60% of Americans currently disapprove of how Trump is handling his job vs. 37% who approve. That puts the president's net approval rating at -23% — near his all-time low. Trump is earning even lower marks on voters' top issue this year: the cost of living . Shortly after he returned to office, roughly equal numbers of Americans approved and disapproved of how the president was handling inflation. But today — as tariffs and the Iran war help drive prices up — 70% disapprove and 25% approve . That's a 45-point gap. President Trump arrives to speak at a campaign rally at F&M Bank Arena on Oct. 10, 2026, in Clarksville, Tenn. AP Photo/Alex Brandon Democrats aren't particularly popular. But for the party in power, it may be hard to overcome this level of dissatisfaction with the status quo. That's why, when pollsters ask their so-called generic ballot question — If an election for U.S. Congress were held today, which party's candidate would you vote for in your district? — Americans are currently giving Democrats a substantial lead of 9 percentage points , on average. Making matters worse for Republicans, that lead has expanded as swing voters who favored Trump in 2024 — including some Latinos and independents — say they're planning to vote Democratic. To put a 9-point lead in perspective, Democrats were leading by an average of 7.5 points on the generic ballot at this point in 2018, with Trump as president and Republican majorities in the House and Senate. On Election Day, they picked up 41 seats and flipped the House. If the polls are right, Democrats might win control of the House again. The path to a Republican House But are the polls right? Recently, Republicans have pointed to some surprising survey results on the Senate side — including Democratic leads in rural red states such as Iowa , Kansas and Nebraska — to argue that pollsters might be misjudging public sentiment. They're not wrong to say the polls have missed in the past. Polling errors are commonplace; they happen in most elections. But they tend to be random and to change directions from one cycle to another . The Trump era has been a little different. In each of the three presidential contests that Trump himself has competed in, the final average of polls conducted before Election Day underestimated Republicans' performance in the popular vote by an average of 3.8 percentage points, according to data journalist Nate Silver . The theory is that a phenomenon called nonresponse bias — in which Democratic voters are more eager or available to respond to pollsters than Republican voters — might have made Democratic support look stronger than it actually was. Pollsters try to adjust for this by weighting their results — that is, using statistical methods to give less weight to respondents who are overrepresented demographically and more weight to respondents who are underrepresented demographically. But it's difficult to predict in advance who will show up on Election Day. This time around, there are signs that rural Republicans are not responding to pollsters in certain states . Could that mean Republican candidates in those places will outperform their polling? Possibly. But experts say it may also mean that rural Republicans are less supportive of the GOP than they were in 2024 — potentially voting Democratic or staying home on Nov. 3. A voter walks toward his polling place. REUTERS / REUTERS After all, there's been virtually no polling bias toward Democrats in Trump era elections when Trump himself wasn't on the ballot. In fact, the polls since 2016 have overestimated Republican support in midterm elections (by an average of 0.2%) and off-year, special and runoff elections (by an average of 1.3%), according to Silver . Either way, pollsters aren't seeing signs of this rural effect in most states — and even if they were, it might make only a minor dent in Democrats' 9-point national lead . Redistricting is the other Republican advantage. House redistricting efforts typically take place every 10 years, after each new census reveals changes in population distribution. But last summer, Trump successfully pushed GOP legislators in Texas to pass new congressional district boundaries five years earlier than normal to help Republicans win five additional House seats in 2026. This kicked off a tit-for-tat cycle that saw nine states adopt new congressional maps for the midterms — some to benefit Democrats, others Republicans. Now that the dust has settled, Cook projects that Republicans could win nine seats because of redistricting (in Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee and Texas), while Democrats could win five (in California and Utah). If that plays out, it would net the GOP four seats overall. It's not what Republicans initially hoped to gain from gerrymandering. "We're not gonna win all 13 of those redistricted seats. That's correct. We're not," GOP House Majority Whip Tom Emmer of Minnesota told Axios recently . But it's also not nothing. The hope for the GOP is that some combination of polling error and redistricting boost — along with a late influx of hundreds of millions of dollars to help defend districts Trump won in 2024 — will be just enough to preserve their slim House majority. articles.title: Binance's $6.3 billion hack is the biggest known crypto theft ever
articles.summary: The estimated $6.3 billion theft reported Thursday by crypto exchange Binance isn't the first time the industry has dealt with a major, unexpected incident in which large sums of customer assets are frozen , spurring a rout in crypto stocks. It may bring to mind crypto's more turbulent days, such as the collapse of FTX, though in that full-on meltdown , with an initial shortfall of $8 billion to $8.9 billion, the Binance rival’s own founder, Sam Bankman-Fried, was charged with the heist. Bankman-Fried was convicted of fraud in 2024 and sentenced to 25 years in prison. Yahoo Finance The Binance hack has rattled crypto markets: Bitcoin ( BTC ), other digital assets, and related stocks have sunk over the last 24 hours. The company has temporarily suspended customer withdrawals, and outside investigators are racing to track down the stolen funds. The company said it has successfully frozen 44% of stolen funds with the help of stablecoin issuers and "will cover all losses" from the incident. As far as comparable hacks go, this most recent theft towers over the rest in terms of scale. Here are four major crypto thefts you may not have heard of. Nearly $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025 Hackers linked to North Korea stole nearly $1.5 billion in ether from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit. The attackers manipulated a transaction approval process, allowing them to redirect assets from a supposedly secure wallet. $625 million on Ronin Network compromised in March 2022 Hackers compromised the security infrastructure of Ronin Network, a blockchain connected to Axie Infinity, a then-popular online crypto game. Hackers stole approximately 173,600 ether and 25.5 million USDC tokens . US authorities weeks later attributed the attack to North Korean hackers , known as the Lazarus Group. $611 million nabbed from Poly Network in August 2021 In 2021, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Poly Network, a platform designed to transfer crypto across different blockchains. In an unusual development, the attacker subsequently returned nearly all of the stolen assets, claiming they did it " for fun " and to expose a software vulnerability. $3.5 billion lost from Chinese bitcoin mining pool LuBian in December 2020 (Unconfirmed) A crypto wallet tied to a little-known Chinese bitcoin mining pool called LuBian may have been the victim of what would be the second-largest crypto theft ever recorded after Binance's breach. LuBian apparently lost more than 127,426 BTC after hackers potentially exploited weaknesses in how the company generated its private keys, according to findings reported by blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence. The suspected theft wasn't identified until August of last year. Follow David Hollerith on X @DsHollers . articles.title: Judge opens probe into potential DOJ misconduct over Trump's golf course plans
articles.summary: A federal judge has opened an investigation into concerns that the Trump administration lied to her in the ongoing legal battle over President Trump’s desire to redevelop East Potomac Golf Links. Friday’s hearing became the latest fiery courtroom clash between U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes and the Department of Justice (DOJ), which repeatedly took issue with the judge’s lines of questioning and pushed back on any suggestion that information was wrongly withheld. “The court will open a formal inquiry into whether agency officials and employees, including agency attorneys and DOJ attorneys, have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules,” the judge said. A preservationist group and local golfers are suing to stop major redevelopments at East Potomac Park, the longtime home of a public golf course along the edge of the nation’s capital. Trump has repeatedly expressed a desire to redevelop it into a championship-style course, and in recent days, he has said the site will close beginning Nov. 15 so the project can proceed. The president’s comments — and recent work to cut down hundreds of trees — have escalated the legal fight. In a flurry of recent hearings in Reyes’s courtroom, the judge whom former President Biden appointed has repeatedly torn into DOJ attorneys about their representations on the status of the project, suggesting they were telling her something different and not to believe the president. Reyes began on Friday by reminding the DOJ’s No. 3 official, Stanley Woodward, about professional ethics rules he is bound to follow as an attorney practicing before the court. As they continued to spar, the judge at one point told Woodward to “finish that thought internally” and to “talk about it at drinks with your friends.” “We’re not on TV. I’m not a pundit,” Woodward pushed back at another point, also suggesting some of the judge’s questioning was blocked under executive privilege. The judge announced she was opening the investigation after learning that the government has been working to submit the redesign plan to the National Capital Planning Commission, which examines major government projects in the Washington area. Reyes expressed frustration that the DOJ hadn’t previously told her about it. She said she’ll conduct the investigation herself or appoint a special master to do so. As of now, the judge has restricted further tree-clearing at the golf course and has implemented new notice requirements, but she hasn’t yet outright blocked the planned closure. “Trust but verify … no longer,” Reyes warned the government. articles.title: 'I'm deeply hurt': Christa Pike speaks after surviving lethal injection
articles.summary: Christa Pike is speaking out publicly for the first time since she survived an execution attempt by the state of Tennessee on Sept. 30. "There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," Pike said in her first public statement since the execution attempt, which her legal team shared Friday. "My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer, and spent 30 years on death row. Two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital failed to kill her during the state's execution attempt last month. She was taken to the hospital, where she received lifesaving care. Slemmer's mother, May Martinez , described the situation as a "mess" and said she was left without justice. “I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position,” Pike said. "I continue to think about my victim's family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured." Pike's legal team described the outcome as "unprecedented" and said it has raised questions about what happens next in her case. "I don't know why I survived that night," Pike added. "I don't know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time. And I am holding on to the love and kindness of so many people who have reminded me that I am not alone." Pike's survival has brought intense scrutiny to Tennessee's execution procedures. Gov. Bill Lee suspended the one remaining execution scheduled for this year, and the state's top prison official, Correction Commissioner Frank Strada, is stepping down at the end of October. Pike's lawyers said the resignation was "justified, but it does nothing to help Christa now. They said the botched execution "reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," they said in a statement issued earlier this month, according to ABC News . Pike has been held at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center since Oct. 10, where she has been behind bars for more than 30 years. She continues to receive medical care in the prison's infirmary. "I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger," her statement read. "But healing is not the same as being okay." What was Christa Pike's condition after the botched execution? When Pike arrived at the hospital, her arms were "swollen, burned and blistered," her lawyers wrote in a legal filing on Oct. 2. Her lawyers believe the IV lines were placed incorrectly or her veins burst, so that some or all of the drug went into the tissue of her arms instead of her bloodstream. Her condition was so severe in the following days, after the execution attempt, that it was believed that she may be brain-dead and could be removed from life support the following day, Randy Spivey, one of her attorneys, said during a press conference on Oct. 7. "On Tuesday, to the shock of everyone … Christa woke up and began talking," he said. Spivey added that Pike is feeling "angry and confused" after waking up in the hospital and is still dealing with major physical problems from the failed execution, including a blood clot, pneumonia and swelling that has left her unable to use both of her arms. "Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery," her legal team wrote in a court filing on Oct. 6. Dr. Joel Zivot, a medical expert who has consulted with Pike's legal team, told the Associated Press that the latest update "bodes well for a good recovery," but said that the full picture of her long-term health will not be clear for some time. "She has recovered to a certain degree that she's able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk," he said. "There's still a lot of bad things that can happen here." Pike, pictured in 2007, is conscious and speaking in the hospital, according to her legal team. via REUTERS / REUTERS Deborah Denno, a criminologist and professor at Fordham Law School, told the BBC that she was "absolutely astonished" that Pike was conscious and speaking. "They did everything they were supposed to do as part of the execution process, and it simply didn't work," she said. "This has never happened before." Dr. Zivot told the BBC that her survival was "unusual," adding, "Most people who get lethal injection die from it. In fact, pretty well everyone, except Christa." Seattle University Law Professor Michael Russo told the Associated Press, "There's nobody else in the history of the death penalty in this country who has gone through what she's been through." The incident with Pike comes a handful of months after the botched attempt to execute Tony Carruthers . In May, Tennessee stopped the execution of Carruthers after staff placed an IV into his right arm, but were unable to insert a secondary IV line. What happens next? All executions in Tennessee are paused for now. Pike's lawyers have called for her sentence to be commuted. State officials have not said whether they will try to execute Pike again, and Gov. Lee has not indicated that he plans to intervene in Pike's case. Lee had denied Pike's clemency before the execution attempt. "I think at the very least the governor should commute Ms. Pike's death sentence to a life sentence," attorney Stephen Ferrell told CNN's State of the Union earlier this month. "We don't know what her physical state will be, but it is clear that she has endured a torturous attempt at executing her." Dr. Zivot said it remains unclear how much pentobarbital entered Pike's system, how much remained in her blood after the injection and what effects she could still experience as she recovers. "I would not, in any way, say at this point that all the big risks are behind her," he said. Professor Russo doubted whether the Supreme Court would stop the state from trying again on double jeopardy grounds — the constitutional protection against being tried or punished twice for the same offense — should it decide to do so. He said, "I think what this Supreme Court would say is, her sentence was to die — to be executed — not to suffer an attempt at execution." "We're in uncharted territory," Robin Maher, executive director of the nonprofit Death Penalty Information Center, told USA Today . "The U.S. Supreme Court has not decided whether a second execution attempt would violate the Constitution since 1947. These are questions that have never needed to be asked before, and no one knows the answers." articles.title: Netanyahu's party claims election was stolen as results show him losing majority
articles.summary: Tel Aviv — Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party alleged Thursday that Israel's election earlier in the week was stolen by Arab-majority parties, helped by foreign funding that amounted to vote-buying, as final results showed Netanyahu's bloc has lost its majority in Israel's parliament, the Knesset. Israel's Arab-majority parties had their highest turnout ever in Tuesday's election, winning an unprecedented 19 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Their success is one of the main reasons Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority and can't now form a new government. The final election results show the far-right wing bloc's share of Knesset seats fell from 68 to 53. Israel's Arab minority, also called Palestinian citizens of Israel, makes up about 20% of the country's population. "Israel's elections have been stolen," Netanyahu's Likud party declared in a statement Thursday, claiming "an attack on democracy aimed at leading to a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel, and the overthrow of the right-wing government to cause a withdrawal and defeat of the IDF (Israeli military) on all fronts — first and foremost, Iran." The four parties that make up the main bloc opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats, so they would need some support from the Arab parties to try to form a coalition government, assuming none of the lawmakers currently aligned with Netanyahu's bloc defect. The heads of Israel's two biggest Arab parties, which collectively won 19 seats, have said they would be willing to help the main opposition bloc oust Netanyahu from power. Most of the Jewish-led parties that oppose Netanyahu vowed before the election not to rely on support from Arab parties to form a government, however, leaving a question mark over whether they might now be willing to cooperate to build a coalition to unseat the incumbent prime minister. "No basis to the claims regarding a systematic compromise" The Shin Bet, Israel's internal security agency, said it had opened an investigation into possible foreign influence in the election, but the scope of that investigation has not been made clear. "An investigation of this type is also focused and bounded, and does not cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote democratically and legally," the agency said in a Thursday statement. The Acting Director-General of the Central Elections Committee, Din Livne, said in a letter to a committee member on Thursday that "there is no basis to the claims regarding a systematic compromise of the integrity of the elections." Israel media reports said one of the allegations the Shin Bet investigation would consider was whether Qatar had sent money to Arab parties in order to increase turnout among Arab Israeli voters. Qatar's foreign ministry has denied the accusation. "We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome," ministry spokesperson Majid Al-Ansari said. "Qatar should not be used as a scapegoat for the political failures of certain Israeli politicians." "An improper influence operation?" While vote counting is now officially complete, the election results must still be certified and sent to President Issac Herzog before a new parliament can be sworn in and the process of forming a new government begins. Gadi Eisenkot, head of the centrist Yashar party and the top candidate to replace Netanyahu as prime minister, said he was worried that Netanyahu could be using the allegation of a stolen election to justify delaying or disqualifying the results. "Netanyahu, who has accustomed himself to dealing with reality through lies, consciousness engineering, and the spreading of chaos, is leading alongside his partners an improper influence operation on the Israeli public aimed at delaying the publication of the election results on time and creating fictitious delegitimization of the activity of the 26th Knesset," Eisenkot said Thursday in a social media post. Once the new Knesset is sworn in — even without a new government decided on —   Eisenkot's bloc, along with the Arab parties, could begin passing laws given that they will control a majority in the parliament. Netanyahu, who President Trump endorsed enthusiastically , will remain in his post as a caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. If the parties cannot negotiate to form a new coalition government, then the country would have to hold the election all over again, and Netanyahu would remain the prime minister in the interim. articles.title: U.S. scraps G20 group photo after European diplomats refuse to pose with Russia's Lavrov
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies appeared far apart on critical global security issues as they began meeting Friday in Atlanta, after European objections to Russia’s participation forced the U.S. hosts to cancel the traditional group photo. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pulled the plug after several European officials threatened to boycott or walk out of the snapshot that often kicks off such gatherings. But he still opened the talks with an appeal for unity on the issues that threaten international security and trade. “We are in a critical moment,” Rubio told his colleagues. “We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises.” He pointed to disruptions to global energy and food supplies , trade and freedom of navigation and said many are posing “severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.” Yet there was no sign that the G20 diplomats could come to consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face. Among them are the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran , U.S. tariffs and Chinese machinations in the South China Sea . All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel as well as uncertainty about trade. No joint statement expected from the diplomats' meeting Diplomats who attended the opening session described it as cordial but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland's membership in the G20. Those disagreements, which also include the Trump administration's not inviting G20 member South Africa over the objections of others, will likely prevent the foreign ministers from producing a joint communique when the meetings wrap up Saturday, participants said. That did not surprise Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, who was representing his country in its first time as a guest at a G20 meeting. “We have wars going on and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it’s very difficult to agree a common line,” he told reporters. Several participants, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to discuss the closed-door talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds and to work to make next month's G20 leaders summit hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida a success. Russia's presence at G20 gathering roils Europeans Already poor prospects for the talks worsened when the Europeans balked at being photographed with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. Rubio decided to scrap the picture because he thought the controversy would be a distraction, according to two U.S. officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance. However, the State Department announced Friday that it had approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot air defense interceptors for Ukraine. Lavrov, when asked about the planned three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. next month, told Russian reporters that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s position regarding long-range strikes against Russia “doesn’t help preparation for the talks.” Moscow will not allow a situation in which Ukraine poses a “military threat to legitimate security interests of the Russian Federation,” he said. Lavrov also said Russia sees no point in inviting Poland to join the G20 meeting, adding that it “violates the principles of diplomacy” and the country “adds nothing” to the grouping. Sikorski, whose country is a strong ally of neighboring Ukraine, earlier said, “I am not the only one who does not want to be photographed with Lavrov.” British Foreign Secretary Ed Milliband explicitly called out Lavrov, saying that “if we are serious about our values and our interests we must also work harder to secure just and lasting peace in Ukraine.” “An assault not only on Ukraine but on us all — trampling international law, sovereignty and self determination — core principles on which we all depend,” he said. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said “there is no normality with Russia” but “we must exchange the controversies at the table here,” the German news agency dpa reported. He added that “we also must not send falsely optimistic signals.” Lavrov has traveled only infrequently to NATO member states since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and resulting severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow, and it is unclear if Russian President Vladimir Putin will accept Trump’s invitation to attend the G20 leaders summit at his Miami golf club in December. G20 member South Africa was not invited Ukraine, which is not a G20 member but was invited to attend previous such meetings, was not invited this year as U.S. officials said they made a conscious choice to include only formal members of the group. Poland is seeking formal membership with U.S. support. But missing from the invite list was South Africa, a G20 founding member and the only African country in the group. South Africa is embroiled in several bitter disputes with the Trump administration, and when it chaired the G20 last year, top U.S. officials, including Trump and Rubio, shunned the meetings it hosted. “We have consistently maintained that our nonparticipation is not voluntary,” said Phindile Kunene, spokesperson for South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola. Kunene welcomed support from other G20 members that had expressed reservations about the exclusion and said South Africa was ready to participate “on an equal footing with other members” when Britain takes over the presidency next year. The Iran war hangs over the G20 event The U.S. has said a top priority for the meeting is resolving differences over issues related to freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz , the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the South China Sea. The topic will include discussions on Iran, Russia-Ukraine and China and its smaller neighbors. But hanging over the meeting is the prospect of new U.S. military intervention in Iran, which has put the region, including G20 member Saudi Arabia, on edge. Rubio met on the sidelines with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, as well as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has been a key mediator. The Associated Press has reported that U.S. officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military strikes against Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections and the possibility that Iran will retaliate against them. ___ Associated Press writers Michelle Gumede in Johannesburg, South Africa, Claudia Ciobanu in Warsaw, Poland, Geir Moulson in Berlin, Jill Lawless in London and Farnoush Amiri in New York contributed. articles.title: 一片下跌声中，OpenAI大幅削减融资金额，从300亿降到200亿
articles.summary: OpenAI将新一轮融资目标削减100亿美元至约200亿美元，估值也从1.4万亿美元下调至1.25万亿美元。 据媒体援引多位知情人士报道，OpenAI要求投资者在周五前作出认购承诺，但由于部分投资者调低了认购额度，截至周五的首批认购资金预计不足200亿美元。 周五，纳斯达克100指数下跌3.5%，二级市场的AI抛售潮和头号对手Anthropic即将上市，给这轮融资蒙上阴影。 从“IPO前最后机会”到收缩目标 上月，OpenAI还计划以1.4万亿美元估值融资300亿美元，并将其定位为投资者在明年IPO前入股的最后机会。公司以7月以来营收快速增长为由，把估值从8520亿美元大幅上调。首席财务官Sarah Friar此前曾向员工表示，上市窗口预计在2027年，具体日期未定。 此后科技股遭遇猛烈抛售，市场对AI支出的节奏和规模愈发担忧，OpenAI随之收敛了目标。一位OpenAI支持者说，融资启动时正值AI交易火热，没想到市场急剧逆转，令其措手不及。 需求降温早有迹象。据媒体此前报道，摩根士丹利与旧金山科技基金Dragoneer曾以1.4万亿美元的投前估值，向该行私人财富客户推介OpenAI，反响明显不及以往。“完全没有人争抢，以前每次都是一片哄抢。”一位知情人士说。部分投资者已大量参与过OpenAI历轮融资，如今已有点“消化不良”。 OpenAI的资金需求依然庞大。公司今年3月刚完成1220亿美元融资，目前估值为8520亿美元，但其用于训练和运行模型的算力支出计划，资金需求是3月这笔融资的数倍。 阿联酋财团领衔 知情人士称，包括国家支持的科技基金MGX在内的阿联酋投资财团，预计将成为本轮最大出资方。作为交易的一部分，OpenAI将获得一项选择权，可租用该地区新建的算力。 Founders Fund、Coatue、红杉资本和Andreessen Horowitz等风投机构，以及孙正义旗下的软银，也计划参与。 本轮资金将分批到位。由于部分投资者调低了认购额度，截至周五的首批认购资金预计不足200亿美元。随后OpenAI还将面向富裕个人发售，估值同为1.25万亿美元。一位知情人士称，这部分资金有望将本轮总额补至200亿美元左右。 Anthropic分流资金与关注 OpenAI还要与Anthropic争夺投资者。Anthropic预计下月以1.5万亿美元或更高估值上市，正在吸走市场的资金和注意力。部分投资者表示，倾向于等Anthropic完成IPO，再决定是否投资其对手。 同时持有两家公司头寸的洛克菲勒家族办公室首席投资官Jimmy Chang认为，两家公司IPO前景的不确定性正在压制美国股市。“市场需要看到一次成功的IPO，这些公司需要资金。” OpenAI、红杉资本、Founders Fund和软银均拒绝置评，MGX、Coatue和Andreessen Horowitz未立即回复置评请求。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黑石：Anthropic在IPO后或只能获得“垃圾”评级
articles.summary: 黑石告诉投资者，Anthropic上市后可能无法立即获得投资级评级，预计主要评级机构将给予其“较高档”的垃圾级评级。 媒体援引知情人士消息称，黑石是向Anthropic最新一笔630亿美元芯片融资交易的投资者传达这一信息的。若评级落在垃圾级，Anthropic为逾8000亿美元的算力计划融资将更加复杂。 周五，美国科技股在报道发布后跌至日内低点，纳斯达克100指数收跌3.5%。此前，亚马逊和英特尔的财报已加剧市场对AI热潮可持续性的担忧，美股当天早已大幅走低。 投资级预期落空 知情人士称，过去几个月，黑石一直告诉投资伙伴，预计Anthropic将在年底前拿到投资级评级。但根据主要评级机构给出的指引，黑石近期改口称，Anthropic获得BB区间或以上评级的可能性更大。 按标普和惠誉的评级体系，BBB-及以上为投资级，BB+及以下为投机级，市场俗称“垃圾级”。 这一评级对Anthropic至关重要。公司周一提交上市申请，下月可能完成有史以来规模最大的IPO。招股书勾勒了一项“大胆但理性”的计划：从现在到2045年，在算力基础设施上投入逾8000亿美元。 目前，Anthropic持有逾1120亿美元现金及等价物，投资者预计IPO还将募资约1000亿美元。 投资级评级能让Anthropic以更低利率借钱，为这些项目融资。而很多保险公司、养老基金按规定只能投资级为主，或者限制持有垃圾级债务的规模。主体一旦掉到BB+及以下，它能触及的资金池将明显收窄，利率也会更高。 “关键在于能否获得信贷，这一点非常重要……如果（Anthropic）不是投资级，信贷成本就会上升，这对谁都不是好事。”一位专注美国科技股的基金经理说。对于当天的股市抛售，这位基金经理的评价是：“外面简直是一场血洗。” Anthropic和竞争对手OpenAI的银行家都在游说几家最大的评级机构，希望两家AI公司上市后获得投资级评级。对企业借贷成本影响更大的三大评级机构——惠誉、穆迪和标普，至今尚未正式给予Anthropic任何信用评级。 “北极星”：借博通的信用融资 最新这笔630亿美元的交易代号“北极星”（Project North Star），华尔街银行已于本周早些时候完成交割。资金将用于Anthropic租赁谷歌1.5GW的芯片。黑石担任锚定投资者，并与出资银行合作，将债务转售给其他投资者。 交易结构显示出Anthropic对供应商信用的依赖。逾420亿美元优先级贷款由博通担保，博通参与联合开发这批芯片，拥有A档高位的投资级评级，这是Anthropic能够拿到这笔融资的重要因素。机构投资者青睐优先级债务，因为一旦违约，其受偿顺序排在次级贷款之前。 另有180亿美元次级债务以Anthropic的租赁付款为支撑，贷款人因此更直接地承担Anthropic的信用风险。据《金融时报》此前报道，黑石旗下基金以超过10%的高收益率认购了其中90亿美元。 这部分次级债务获得Kroll Bond Rating Agency（KBRA）给予的BB+评级，展望为正面，较四个月前类似交易“大天空”（Big Sky）的稳定展望略有改善；晨星DBRS则给予BB评级。 Anthropic、黑石、KBRA、晨星DBRS和标普均拒绝置评，惠誉和穆迪未回复置评请求。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 中国10月官方制造业PMI 49.3，非制造业PMI 49.7
articles.summary: 中国10月制造业与非制造业景气水平均有所回落，但 10月大型制造业企业继续扩张，铁路运输、水上运输、邮政、互联网软件及信息技术服务等行业商务活动指数均位于较高景气区间。 10月31日，国家统计局数据显示， 10月制造业PMI为49.3%，比上月下降0.8个百分点，制造业景气水平有所回落。 与此同时， 非制造业商务活动指数为49.7%，比上月下降0.5个百分点，非制造业景气水平有所下降。资本市场服务、保险、房地产等行业商务活动指数均低于临界点。 整体来看，综合PMI产出指数为49.7%，比上月下降1.0个百分点。 国家统计局服务业调查中心首席统计师霍丽慧指出， “十一”假期前部分需求提前释放，以及国际环境复杂多变，是导致制造业景气度回落的主要因素 。 尽管整体景气度承压，但经济运行中不乏结构性亮点。高技术制造业继续保持扩张，凸显新质生产力发展态势良好；同时，受长假消费提振，部分服务业表现活跃。 服务业商务活动指数微降至50.0%的临界点。 霍丽慧解读称，金融行业商务活动指数回落且幅度较大，是本月服务业景气度略有回落的主要原因。 此外，资本市场服务、保险和房地产等行业的景气度均低于临界点。不过，与“十一”假期出行消费密切相关的铁路运输、住宿、文化体育娱乐等行业回升明显，水上运输、邮政及互联网软件等行业更是维持在55.0%以上的高景气区间。 中国制造业采购经理指数运行情况 10月份，制造业采购经理指数（PMI）为49.3%，比上月下降0.8个百分点，制造业景气水平有所回落。 从企业规模看 ，大型企业PMI为50.2%，比上月下降0.4个百分点，仍高于临界点；中、小型企业PMI分别为48.4%和47.5%，比上月下降1.3个和1.4个百分点，低于临界点。 从分类指数看 ，构成制造业PMI的5个分类指数中，供应商配送时间指数高于临界点；生产指数、新订单指数、原材料库存指数和从业人员指数低于临界点。 生产指数为49.8%，比上月下降1.9个百分点，表明制造业生产活动有所放缓。 新订单指数为49.4%，比上月下降1.1个百分点，表明制造业市场需求景气度下降。 原材料库存指数为48.4%，比上月上升0.2个百分点，表明制造业主要原材料库存量降幅有所收窄。 从业人员指数为48.4%，与上月持平，表明制造业企业用工景气度总体平稳。 供应商配送时间指数为50.2%，比上月上升0.1个百分点，表明制造业原材料供应商交货时间加快。 中国非制造业采购经理指数运行情况 10月份，非制造业商务活动指数为49.7%，比上月下降0.5个百分点，非制造业景气水平有所下降。 分行业看 ，建筑业商务活动指数为48.0%，比上月下降2.3个百分点；服务业商务活动指数为50.0%，比上月下降0.2个百分点。 从服务业行业看 ， 铁路运输、水上运输、邮政、互联网软件及信息技术服务等行业商务活动指数均位于55.0%以上较高景气区间 ； 资本市场服务、保险、房地产等行业商务活动指数均低于临界点。 新订单指数为44.4%，比上月下降2.1个百分点，表明非制造业市场需求景气水平回落 。分行业看，建筑业新订单指数为40.0%，比上月下降5.7个百分点；服务业新订单指数为45.2%，比上月下降1.5个百分点。 投入品价格指数为51.5%，比上月下降1.0个百分点，表明非制造业企业用于经营活动的投入品价格总体水平涨幅收窄 。分行业看，建筑业投入品价格指数为52.4%，比上月下降1.6个百分点；服务业投入品价格指数为51.4%，比上月下降0.8个百分点。 销售价格指数为49.5%，比上月下降0.8个百分点，表明非制造业企业销售价格总体水平有所回落 。分行业看，建筑业销售价格指数为48.9%，比上月上升0.4个百分点；服务业销售价格指数为49.6%，比上月下降1.0个百分点。 从业人员指数为46.0%，比上月上升0.1个百分点，表明非制造业企业用工景气度略有改善 。分行业看，建筑业从业人员指数为42.0%，比上月下降2.3个百分点；服务业从业人员指数为46.7%，比上月上升0.5个百分点。 业务活动预期指数为54.7%，比上月下降0.8个百分点，仍高于临界点，表明非制造业企业对市场发展保持信心。分行业看，建筑业业务活动预期指数为52.3%，比上月下降3.1个百分点；服务业业务活动预期指数为55.2%，比上月下降0.3个百分点。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 雪上加霜！科技股“认清现实”的一周
articles.summary: 谷歌、亚马逊、英特尔的财报接连让市场失望，本周AI交易的裂痕明显扩大。周五（10月30日）英特尔股价暴跌29%，创有史以来最大单日跌幅；纳斯达克综合指数下跌2.9%，是6月以来最差的一天，10月也将成为纳指一年多来表现最差的月份。 此前数月，AI交易的风险主要暴露在负债沉重的小公司身上，巨头凭借丰厚利润稳住了华尔街。本周，情况变了：谷歌搜索广告增长放缓，亚马逊自由现金流大幅转负，英特尔预计PC销售将长期低迷。据FactSet，“七巨头”第三季度盈利增速预计将低于标普500其余成分股。 市场追问的问题，已经从AI需求有多大，变成谁来为AI买单。高盛Delta One主管Rich Privorotsky写道： “资本成本已经客观地重新定价，而且没有显而易见的解决办法。” 巨头财报接连失守 本周初，Anthropic提交的IPO文件显示营收飙升，一度提振市场情绪，但随后的巨头财报给市场泼了冷水。 Alphabet 搜索广告增长放缓，部分原因是“AI模式”查询的冲击，公司还表示2027年资本开支将“显著”增加。周四股价下跌13%，创历史最差单日表现，市值蒸发约4890亿美元，伯克希尔·哈撒韦等大股东损失惨重。 亚马逊 周四盘后公布的营收不及预期，单季自由现金流为-335亿美元，比预期差四倍多；资本开支激增至773亿美元，同期新增长期债务481亿美元。周五股价下跌7%。 英特尔 预计第四季度营收150亿至160亿美元，低于市场预期的172.9亿美元，并表示今年不会实现正现金流。公司还预计PC销售将长期放缓，原因是AI热潮推高了存储芯片价格。英特尔周五收跌29%，盘中跌幅一度达29.7%，为彭博自1982年有数据以来的最大日内跌幅。两大股东美国政府和英伟达的账面持仓合计蒸发逾170亿美元。 微软 Azure增长48%，但商业订单下降12%。财报发布约12小时后，这家唯一获AAA评级的科技公司启动250亿美元债券发行，为2017年以来首次。 周五抛售蔓延至整个科技板块：七巨头全线收跌，存储芯片、半导体和新兴云服务商（neocloud）股价重挫，Reddit下跌26%，比特币跌超5%。OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners首席投资官Peter Boockvar说： “裂缝之间未必有关联，但裂缝足够多时，路面最终会不会塌陷？” 从“需求买单”到“谁来买单” 巨头赚得足够多，市场此前一直容忍其大举投资。Tema ETFs投资策略主管Paisley Nardini说，此前“花钱代表对这轮建设的信心，会得到奖励”，而“突然之间，花钱被视为逆风”。 转折始于Meta。10月21日，Meta公布第四季度资本开支490亿至590亿美元，扣除股息后自由现金流为负，并在文件中警示最早从2026年秋季起需要“筹集数千亿美元”。10月26日，Meta启动最高975亿美元的股权融资，英伟达、AMD和博通表示有意认购最多50亿美元。同日Anthropic提交的S-1文件显示，其算力账单约为7800亿至8100亿美元。据彭博统计，四大科技巨头今年的资本开支将接近7500亿美元，“投资者已不再对回报照单全收”。 信用市场更早发出了信号。9月初至10月中旬，超大规模云厂商和AI相关公司没有发行一笔投资级债券，CoreWeave无担保债券利差突破1000个基点。本周超大规模云厂商CDS再创新高；由于得州冻结新项目，银行搁置了为Anthropic旗下150亿美元得州数据中心发行的垃圾债。高盛信用策略师指出，AI领域违约风险自1月以来已增至三倍。 Baird科技策略师Ted Mortonson说，巨额融资对华尔街银行是好事，但让基金经理们“吓得魂飞魄散”，“我的建议是先避开”。Truist Advisory Services首席投资官Keith Lerner则表示：“看空的逻辑是，盈利峰值比我们想象的更近。” 指数之下的剧烈轮动 截至周四，标普500指数本月仍上涨约0.9%，距纪录高位仅几个百分点，但内部分化剧烈。纳指100本月下跌约3.3%，成分股市值蒸发逾1.2万亿美元。七巨头10月累计下跌超6%，新兴云服务商跌37%，高盛“最易受AI冲击”的股票篮子则上涨逾15%。 10月29日，谷歌暴跌拖累标普500下跌0.3%，尽管当天有406只成分股上涨。彭博1996年以来的数据显示，此前987个上涨家数不少于400只的交易日，指数无一例外收涨。瑞银交易员称，资金正从拥挤的AI和成长股流向价值股、小盘股、消费及利率敏感型周期股，并未撤离股市。 机构仓位同步收缩。高盛主经纪商数据显示，对冲基金抛售科技股的速度创十余年来最快两周纪录，美股净杠杆降至五年来最低水平。高盛高贝塔动量组合较6月峰值回撤43%，抹去全年涨幅。亚洲方面，三星电子和SK海力士本月跌幅均超16%。 利率、伊朗与中期选举 美联储9月加息后，市场预期还将继续收紧；本月美联储暂停加息，但有两票鹰派反对。美联储主席Kevin Warsh本周表示：“利率直接或间接地影响几乎一切……市场参与者正在区分自己想做的投资。” 地缘风险也在升温。特朗普暗示，下周中期选举后美国可能对伊朗发起新的军事行动。布伦特原油近月期货周五收于每桶117.64美元，接近年内高点，盘中一度触及118美元。美债则走强，10年期收益率跌破4.9%，创六周新低，债市更多将油价飙升视为对经济增长的威胁。中期选举还将决定，美国各地对数据中心的反对声浪在多大程度上会转化为开发限制。 乐观者仍在。Founders 100 ETF基金经理Michael Monaghan认为，若中东局势企稳，市场将“大幅上涨”；即将到来的Anthropic IPO“是撑住整个AI交易的那块积木”。“我们看好，AI交易还没有结束。” 但Privorotsky提醒，风险在于融资约束最终会迫使巨头控制资本开支，“只是目前在支出意向上还看不到这一点”。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 白酒板块业绩还在寻底，市场资金为什么先回来了？
articles.summary: 10月30日午间，白酒板块突然走强：中证白酒指数上涨3.94%，沪深300下跌0.38%，16只样本股中15只上涨，古井贡酒、迎驾贡酒等涨停。与股价形成反差的是，已披露的三季报仍显示行业承压，五粮液、泸州老窖、汾酒和洋河的收入、利润均明显下滑。市场正在交易什么？ 白酒经历多年估值与持仓压缩后，机构配置处于低位，板块内部又出现现金流、分红和经营弹性的差异。科技成长交易拥挤度缓解，资金开始重新比较不同资产的回报结构，白酒因此进入新的配置视野。 一、发生了什么？——三季报仍在恶化，白酒股为什么先涨了？ 1. 白酒三季报：行业调整的深度，超出局部收入转正带来的乐观感 截至10月30日午间，茅台、今世缘尚未披露三季报，已披露的8家重点酒企已足以呈现行业调整深度。Q3单季度收入同比中位数为-18.65%，归母净利润同比中位数为-41.39%；按样本公司合计口径，收入和归母净利润分别下降27.9%和51.4%。收入正增长仅古井、迎驾、口子三家，利润正增长仅迎驾和舍得两家。 全国性酒企压力突出：五粮液Q3收入、归母净利润分别下降37.7%和48.3%，泸州老窖分别下降37.1%和57.0%，汾酒分别下降18.1%和34.5%；洋河收入下降61.1%，单季亏损7.71亿元，较上年同期亏损3.69亿元扩大109%。商务消费收缩、渠道去库存和产品结构下移共同作用，行业利润池仍在收缩。 现金流进一步拉开公司差距。前三季度经营现金流净额/同期归母净利润，五粮液仅约0.5%，洋河约6.3%，口子窖为负；汾酒、古井和迎驾分别约95%、94%和101%。五粮液前三季度归母净利润97.1亿元，经营现金流净额仅0.47亿元，利润兑现与现金回收明显脱节。白酒现金流受回款和付款时点影响，但同一报告期内的巨大差异，已经揭示经营质量分层。 ……

articles.title: 茅台三季度净利增3.78%，增长动力重新转向批发渠道
articles.summary: 贵州茅台在持续调整产品供给、价格和销售渠道后，重新恢复利润增长。 10月30日，贵州茅台披露2026年第三季度报告。第三季度实现营业收入402.67亿元，同比增长3.08%；归母净利润199.51亿元，同比增长3.78%。 相比二季度营收、利润双降，茅台三季度业绩明显改善，利润表现也好于部分机构预期。 不过，这轮业绩修复也有低基数因素。2025年第三季度，茅台已经开始主动控制产品投放，当季营收、归母净利润同比仅增长0.56%和0.48%。 渠道与税费结构的变化，更能解释茅台三季度盈利能力为何环比改善。 今年二季度，茅台主动减少部分产品向经销渠道的投放，避免通过渠道压货完成销售目标。同时，部分非标产品转向代售模式，改变了原有的销售和收入确认节奏。 进入三季度，伴随中秋、国庆备货，传统经销渠道发货有所恢复。 三季度，茅台批发代理收入184.24亿元，环比增长近三成；直销收入218.12亿元，环比略有下降。其中，i茅台收入182.99亿元，与二季度基本持平。 申万宏源10月的渠道调研显示，受访茅台经销商前三季度配额已全部完成，部分提前执行10月配额，回款与发货进度基本匹配，渠道库存维持低位。 武汉京魁科技有限公司董事长肖竹青向华尔街见闻表示，茅台持续关注经销商库存和市场价格变化，在观察到市场价格上涨、供给趋紧后，提前执行部分销售计划，推动三季度销售放量。 “这也是茅台推进市场化改革的体现。通过根据市场行情灵活调整产品投放节奏，茅台希望兼顾上市公司股东回报、地方经济发展需求与经销商盈利，实现各方利益的平衡。”肖竹青说。 渠道结构调整进一步牵动了茅台税费端的变化。 二季度，茅台直销收入占酒类主营业务收入的比例升至约61%，同期税金及附加占营收比例达到17.54%。 8月的业绩说明会上，公司财务总监、董事会秘书余思明曾解释，直销占比提高导致主要产品消费税计税基价增加，同时生产端消费税与终端销售收入确认存在时间差，推高了当期税费负担。 三季度，随着批发代理收入回升，直销占比降至54.2%，税金及附加占营收比例也回落至15.13%，接近一季度水平。 7月飞天茅台提价同样为盈利修复提供支撑。其中，53度500ml飞天茅台销售合同价与i茅台零售价分别上调100元，至1369元和1639元。 不过，受产品结构调整影响，茅台产品整体毛利率并未明显改善。 当前阶段，随着普通飞天等产品销量占比提高，部分高附加值非标产品价格下调，茅台整体吨酒收入承压。 同时，销量增加带动更多已售产品对应的生产成本结转，使营业成本增速高于收入增速。 三季度公司销售毛利率约89.6%，环比仅小幅改善，同比仍然下降。 据第三方平台“今日酒价”披露，10月30日，2026年飞天茅台原箱报1715元/瓶、散瓶报1695元/瓶，一个月内基本持平。往年款略有回落，2025年飞天原箱、散瓶报价均较一个月前回落30元，至1800元和1720元。 三季度业绩回暖，反映出茅台通过调整渠道投放、产品价格和销售结构，已经在一定程度上缓解了此前的经营压力。 随着渠道改革逐步推进，茅台对产品供给和价格的调节更加直接。如何在维持核心产品销售韧性的同时，改善非标产品的市场表现，将成为后续盈利持续修复的重要变量。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 苹果官宣：Apple智能接入阿里千问，11月4日开放测试
articles.summary: 苹果公司在推动其人工智能技术落地全球最大智能手机市场方面迈出关键一步。 北京时间10月31日，苹果公司正式宣布与阿里巴巴集团达成合作，将 大模型“通义千问”整合进中国大陆市场的苹果智能（Apple Intelligence）系统中 。 相关集成功能将于 11月4日随iOS 27.3开发者测试版首发 ，并 计划于12月随系统正式版向中国用户全面推送 。 届时，符合条件的中国iPhone用户可在Siri、写作工具以及视觉智能功能中，直接调用千问的文本与图像理解及内容生成能力。 阿里巴巴集团首席执行官吴泳铭表示，千问将深度融入苹果生态，为中国用户带来全新的智能服务。 不过，首批上线的苹果智能仍面临严格的硬件及合规限制。 该服务目前仅限于符合运行内存要求的特定iPhone机型，iPad与Mac设备暂未列入首批支持范围。 同时，受制于监管审批进度，苹果在今年WWDC 2026上发布的新一代苹果智能及Siri AI等高级功能，暂不向中国大陆市场提供。 功能深度融合，端侧模型主导日常操作 根据官方披露的技术细节，此次随iOS 27.3上线的苹果智能涵盖了 2024年WWDC 发布时的全部基础功能，包括实时翻译、照片消除、写作工具以及生成式表情符号（Genmoji）等。 在日常高频使用场景中，iPhone内置的端侧模型将占据主导地位，以最大限度保障数据处理的安全性与低延迟。 对于更复杂的生成和检索任务，系统将调用云端大模型。在本土化合作框架下，Siri能够直接调用千问的广博知识库来回复用户问答。 用户还可通过Siri分享特定文档和照片向千问提问，或通过相机控制、操作按钮等启用视觉智能功能中的“询问千问”来识别周围环境。 此外，千问也被深度接入系统的“千问创作”（Compose with Qwen）功能中，支持用户基于任意主题从零生成文本或图像内容。据悉，除阿里外， 百度的文心大模型也将参与提供搜索和视觉识别等相关底层能力 。 聚焦隐私护栏，监管合规化初见成效 在推进云端大模型接入的同时，苹果延续了其对数据隐私的严格标准。 千问的集成功能采用用户自主选择（Opt-in）模式 。用户启用该功能后，可通过Apple账户或自有的千问App账户登录。在任何请求、文档和图片发送给千问之前，系统均会先行征得用户同意。 阿里巴巴也明确承诺，不会将用户的请求及生成的回复用于任何模型训练，以确保隐私隔离。 根据中国工信部10月公布的iPhone进网许可信息，苹果的手机端侧模型已在国内完成备案，阿里巴巴的通义千问和通义万相亦在备案之列。 这表明苹果与本地合作伙伴在满足数据安全与生成式AI服务管理规定方面已达成共识，为系统级AI功能的最终落地扫清了关键障碍。 硬件设限严格，长期落地仍面临监管考验 尽管苹果智能落地中国迈出实质性一步，但其高昂的硬件门槛限制了短期内的渗透率。 首批支持该功能的设备仅限iPhone 15 Pro系列、iPhone 16系列及之后的机型，以及iPhone Air和iPhone Duo。 这一限制主要源于AI模型对8GB运行内存（RAM）及7GB本地存储空间（ROM）的硬性要求，较早机型及iPhone 15标准版均无法通过软件升级获得该能力。 从发布到落地，苹果智能在中国的推进历时两年有余。 自2024年6月首度亮相海外，直到2025年2月蔡崇信确认阿里与苹果的合作，其本土化路径才渐趋明朗。尽管近期库克访华加速了测试版的推出，但这场合规拉锯战远未结束。 目前，iPad与Mac的审批进度依然悬而未决，而如何在其合规框架内将WWDC 2026发布的新一代Siri AI完整生态更快地带给中国用户，仍是苹果管理层需要长期应对的核心议题。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 欧洲股市化身“反AI交易”避风港，防御性板块领涨十月行情
articles.summary: 在通胀与经济增长逆风交织的背景下，欧洲股市在10月份凭借稳健的防御性特征脱颖而出，化身为全球市场的“反AI交易”代表，不仅跑赢美股及全球主要基准指数，也为寻求避险的投资者提供了新的资金去处。 10月，欧洲斯托克600指数累计上涨1.9%，创下自6月以来的最佳单月表现，并收复9月份大部分失地 。该指数在当月跑赢标普500指数2.9个百分点，同时领先MSCI全球指数2.8个百分点。 推动此次反弹的核心力量是具备清晰盈利前景、防御性现金流和稳健资产负债表的传统行业 。其中，医疗保健板块录得自1987年以来的最佳单月表现，而食品、饮料和烟草板块更是创下了有史以来的最佳单月涨幅。 这种由避险情绪驱动的板块轮动，凸显出全球资金在风险偏好降温时的配置转变。 随着油价飙升和对人工智能（AI）板块的担忧加剧，欧洲市场与美国科技股的走势进一步脱钩，为投资者在对冲AI相关风险及宏观不确定性时提供了直接的防御性选择。 化身“反AI交易”，防御板块与美股脱钩 欧洲股市在10月份的表现呈现出明显的“反AI交易”特征，价值型买盘在市场出现估值吸引力信号时迅速回归。 彭博数据显示，斯托克600指数与纳斯达克100指数的相关性在10月份降至18%，不足其过去12个月平均水平的一半。 在这种市场环境下，富含防御性公用事业和必需消费品股票的英国富时100指数（FTSE 100）成为了终极的AI对冲工具。 当市场风险偏好消退时，这些股票因其可靠的回报而受到投资者青睐。同时，在油价飙升和AI担忧的推动下，欧洲防御性板块相对于周期性板块走出了多年来最强劲的相对行情。 从技术面来看，斯托克600指数的走势也展现出积极信号。该指数在625点附近的40周移动均线处进行了短暂测试后便迎来反弹，随后突破了自8月历史高点以来形成的下降通道，并重新站上10周和20周均线。 此外据彭博报道， 随着财报季的展开，欧洲企业的盈利表现也拉近了与美国的距离，预计第三季度利润增速将仅略低于标普500指数，这是三年多来欧洲首次如此接近美股的盈利增速。 宏观逆风犹存，英法市场表现分化 尽管整体指数表现稳健，但欧洲面临的宏观背景依然充满挑战， 地缘政治与区域财政风险导致各国市场出现显著分化 。 由于沙特阿拉伯遭遇袭击重燃供应担忧，布伦特原油价格飙升至每桶115美元以上，加剧了通胀焦虑。 在欧洲大陆，法国的动荡局势和财政焦虑情绪推动法国与德国10年期国债收益率利差（OAT-Bund spread）扩大至欧元区债务危机以来的最阔水平。 法国银行和零售商成为主权风险的代理指标，法国CAC 40指数在2026年的落后表现进一步加剧。 受消费者支出担忧影响，零售巨头家乐福（Carrefour）下调了全年业绩目标，该公司首席执行官Alexandre Bompard将当前局势称为“前所未有的”。 相比之下，英国市场提供了积极的对冲。 由于英国预算案中银行税的上调幅度低于市场担忧，劳埃德银行（Lloyds）和巴克莱银行（Barclays）股价应声走高，止住了长达数周的下跌趋势。 不过，随着政治不确定性上升，英国水务股依然处于市场聚光灯下，主要水务公司的空头头寸均出现增加。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
